summary: Pend Oreille County, WA: Gypsy Peak is reported as a patrol point for the 1929 Crowell Ridge lookout; no source read for this record describes a standing structure on the summit.

access.note: Hiked in the Salmo-Priest Wilderness; the road to the Bear Pasture trailhead closes to hikers on August 15 to protect grizzly habitat

visit.trail_note: 3.5 miles one way with 1,800 feet of gain from the Bear Pasture trailhead; no water on the ridge; pick a day with no thunderstorm activity

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Wikipedia gives more than 7,320 feet and WillhiteWeb gives 7,326 feet. The difference is small, and the story reports both figures.

sources.title: Gypsy Peak in Salmo Priest Wilderness

notes_for_editor: Our record lists the agency as Kaniksu National Forest, from the west_us_lookouts list. No page read confirms that for Gypsy Peak, so agency is left out of facts. The Crowell Ridge register page names Colville National Forest for the neighbouring lookout. Confirm the managing forest with the Sullivan Lake Ranger District before publishing. Our record has kind unknown; the sources call the site a patrol point tied to Crowell Ridge. The WillhiteWeb hike page is undated, so the road closure, distance and trail notes need a current check. Crowell staffing (1929 and 1935) is deliberately not attributed to Gypsy Peak. The record's coordinates match GNIS for Gypsy Peak (48.94563, -117.15224), per the local summit table.
